evenements.txt: God creates the heavens and the earth by his word, then man and woman in his image, and places them in the Garden of Eden. All that he has made is very good, and on the seventh day he rests.
The serpent tempts Eve to doubt God's word; Adam and Eve disobey and are cast out of the garden. God already announces the future victory of the woman's offspring over the serpent (Genesis 3:15).
Cain kills his brother Abel out of jealousy. God gives Adam and Eve another son, Seth; with him, they begin to call on the name of the Lord.

The earth is filled with violence. Noah, a righteous man, builds the ark at God's command; his family and the animals are saved from the waters. God makes a covenant with the earth and sets the rainbow as a sign.
Men want to build a tower that reaches to heaven to make a name for themselves. God confuses their language and scatters them across all the earth.

God calls Abram to leave his country for a land he will show him, and promises that through him all the families of the earth will be blessed. Abram believes, and it is credited to him as righteousness (Genesis 15:6).
Abraham intercedes for Sodom. The angels bring Lot and his family out before fire falls on the city; Lot's wife looks back.

evenements.titre: The Birth of Isaac and the Sacrifice on Mount Moriah
evenements.txt: Isaac, the child of the promise, is born to Abraham and Sarah in their old age. Later, God tests Abraham on Mount Moriah and himself provides a ram in place of Isaac.
Jacob obtains Esau's blessing by deception and must flee. God meets him at Bethel, then, twenty years later, wrestles with him at the ford of the Jabbok: Jacob becomes Israel.
Jealous of Joseph, Jacob's favored son, his brothers sell him to merchants. A slave then a prisoner in Egypt, he remains faithful, and the Lord is with him.
Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams and becomes second in command of the kingdom. During the famine, he finds his brothers and forgives them: God has turned evil into good (Genesis 50:20).

evenements.titre: Jacob and His Family in Egypt
evenements.txt: Seventy persons of Jacob's household go down to Egypt and settle in Goshen. Jacob blesses his twelve sons, ancestors of the tribes of Israel.

evenements.titre: Slavery and the Birth of Moses
evenements.txt: A new pharaoh enslaves Israel and commands that Hebrew boys be thrown into the river. Moses is saved from the waters and raised in Pharaoh's court by his daughter.
At Mount Horeb, God speaks to Moses from a bush that burns without being consumed. He reveals his name and sends him to deliver his people.
Pharaoh refuses to let Israel go; God strikes Egypt with ten plagues. On the night of Passover, the blood of the lamb protects the houses of the Israelites, who leave Egypt.

evenements.titre: The Crossing of the Red Sea
evenements.txt: Pursued by the Egyptian army, Israel crosses the sea on dry ground; the waters close over Pharaoh's chariots. Moses and Miriam sing the song of deliverance.
At Sinai, God makes a covenant with Israel and gives the Ten Commandments. While Moses is on the mountain, the people make the golden calf; Moses intercedes for them.
Bezalel and Oholiab, filled with God's Spirit, complete the tabernacle. The cloud of the Lord's glory fills the tent: God dwells among his people.

evenements.titre: The Spies and Forty Years in the Wilderness
evenements.txt: Ten of twelve spies discourage the people from entering Canaan; only Joshua and Caleb trust God. Israel wanders forty years in the wilderness.
After reminding the people of the law, Moses views the Promised Land from Mount Nebo and dies. Joshua succeeds him.
The waters of the Jordan stand still before the ark, and Israel enters the land. The walls of Jericho fall; Rahab, who had hidden the spies, is saved.
The land is divided among the tribes. At Shechem, Joshua renews the covenant: as for me and my household, we will serve the Lord (Joshua 24:15).
Israel forgets God, falls under oppression, cries out to him, and God raises up judges to deliver them: Deborah, Gideon, Jephthah, Samson… Each did what was right in his own eyes.
Ruth the Moabite remains loyal to her mother-in-law Naomi. Boaz redeems her and takes her as his wife; from their son Obed descends King David.
Hannah obtains a son through prayer and dedicates him to God. Samuel hears the Lord's call at Shiloh, then judges Israel and brings the people back to God.
Israel demands a king like the other nations. Saul is anointed by Samuel, but his disobedience causes God to reject him.
Samuel anoints the young shepherd David. Before the Philistine giant Goliath, David advances in the name of the Lord and brings him down with a stone.
David reigns in Hebron then captures Jerusalem and brings the ark there. Through Nathan, God promises him an eternal dynasty and throne, a promise fulfilled in Jesus.
Solomon asks God for wisdom. He builds the temple on Mount Moriah; the glory of the Lord fills it at the dedication.
After Solomon, ten tribes separate under Jeroboam (northern kingdom of Israel); Judah and Benjamin remain under Rehoboam. Jeroboam sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan.
Under Ahab and Jezebel, the worship of Baal spreads throughout Israel. Elijah challenges the prophets of Baal at Carmel, and the fire of the Lord falls on the altar.
Elisha receives a double portion of Elijah's spirit. He multiplies oil, raises the Shunamite woman's son, and heals Naaman the Syrian.
Jonah flees God's call, is swallowed by a great fish, then preaches to Nineveh, which repents. God shows his compassion toward the nations.
Amos denounces injustice; Hosea speaks against Israel's unfaithfulness. In the year of King Uzziah's death, Isaiah sees the glory of God and receives his commission; he will announce Emmanuel.
After a three-year siege, Samaria falls to the Assyrians. The northern kingdom of Israel disappears; its inhabitants are deported, having refused to listen to the prophets.
Sennacherib besieges Jerusalem. Hezekiah spreads the threatening letter before the Lord and prays; the angel of the Lord strikes down the Assyrian camp. Hezekiah is then healed.
During the restoration of the temple, the Book of the Law is found. Young King Josiah humbles himself, renews the covenant, and cleanses the land of idols.
Jeremiah calls Judah to repentance for forty years without being heard. King Jehoiakim burns the scroll of his prophecies; Baruch rewrites it.
Nebuchadnezzar takes young men from Judah to Babylon, among them Daniel and his three friends. They remain faithful to God, and Daniel interprets the king's dream.
The Babylonians capture Jerusalem, burn the temple, and deport the people. Jeremiah weeps over the city but announces the return after seventy years.
By the river Kebar, Ezekiel sees the glory of God. In the valley of dry bones, he announces that God will restore life to his people.
Babylon falls to the Medes and Persians. Daniel continues to pray despite the ban; God shuts the mouth of the lions.

evenements.titre: The Edict of Cyrus and the Return
evenements.txt: As Isaiah and Jeremiah had announced, Cyrus allows the Jews to return and rebuild the temple. The foundations are laid with joy and tears.
Encouraged by the prophets Haggai and Zechariah, Zerubbabel and Joshua resume the work. The temple is completed and dedicated under Darius.
Esther, who has become queen, risks her life to save her people from Haman's plot. The Jewish people are delivered; the Feast of Purim is celebrated.
Ezra, a scribe skilled in the law, returns to Jerusalem. He reads and explains the law to all the people, who weep then rejoice.
Nehemiah, the king's cupbearer, hears of the ruins of Jerusalem, prays and obtains permission to go. Despite opposition, the wall is completed in fifty-two days.
Malachi rebukes a people grown lukewarm and announces a messenger who will prepare the way of the Lord. Then come approximately four hundred years of prophetic silence.

evenements.titre: The Announcements to Zechariah and Mary
evenements.txt: The angel Gabriel announces to Zechariah the birth of John the Baptist, then to Mary that she will conceive by the Holy Spirit the Son of the Most High. Mary responds: I am the Lord's servant.
Because of Augustus' census, Joseph and Mary go up to Bethlehem, where Jesus is born. The angels announce it to the shepherds: A Savior has been born to you.

evenements.titre: Simeon and Anna at the Temple
evenements.txt: Forty days after birth, Jesus is presented at the temple. The aged Simeon and the prophetess Anna recognize in him the salvation promised.

evenements.titre: The Magi and the Flight to Egypt
evenements.txt: Magi from the East worship the child. Warned in a dream, Joseph flees to Egypt with Mary and Jesus to escape Herod, then settles in Nazareth.

evenements.titre: Jesus at the Temple at Twelve
evenements.txt: During a Passover feast, Jesus stays at the temple among the teachers. He tells his parents he must be about his Father's business, then grows in wisdom and in grace.

evenements.titre: John the Baptist and the Baptism of Jesus
evenements.txt: In the fifteenth year of Tiberius, John preaches repentance in the wilderness. Jesus is baptized in the Jordan; the Spirit descends upon him and the Father declares him his beloved Son.
After forty days of fasting, Jesus is tempted by the devil. Each time he answers with Scripture: it is written.
Andrew, Peter, Philip, and Nathanael follow Jesus. At a wedding in Cana, he turns water into wine: this is his first sign.
Jesus explains to Nicodemus that one must be born again. At Jacob's well, he offers living water to a Samaritan woman, and many Samaritans believe.
Jesus announces that the kingdom of God is near. Rejected at Nazareth, he settles in Capernaum, calls fishermen to become fishers of men, and heals many sick.
On a mountain, Jesus teaches the Beatitudes, the Lord's Prayer, and the life of the kingdom. The crowd is amazed at his authority.

evenements.titre: The Choosing of the Twelve Apostles
evenements.txt: After a night of prayer, Jesus chooses twelve apostles to be with him and to send out to preach.
Jesus calms the storm, delivers the demon-possessed man of Gadara, heals a woman sick for twelve years, and raises the daughter of Jairus from the dead.
With five loaves and two fish, Jesus feeds five thousand men. He walks on water and presents himself as the bread of life.
Peter confesses: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God. On a high mountain, Jesus is transfigured before three disciples, with Moses and Elijah.
Jesus declares to Martha: I am the resurrection and the life. He raises Lazarus, dead for four days; the leaders then decide to put him to death.
Jesus enters Jerusalem riding on a colt, fulfilling Zechariah 9:9. The crowd hails him: Hosanna to the Son of David! He drives out the money changers from the temple.
Jesus washes his disciples' feet and institutes the Lord's Supper. In Gethsemane, he prays in anguish; Judas betrays him and the disciples flee.
Condemned by Pilate, Jesus is crucified at Golgotha. He forgives, promises paradise to the penitent criminal, and dies saying: It is finished.
The tomb is empty: Jesus is risen. He appears to Mary Magdalene, to the disciples on the road to Emmaus, to the apostles, and to Thomas, who cries out: My Lord and my God!
Jesus promises the power of the Holy Spirit and ascends to heaven from the Mount of Olives. The disciples pray together; Matthias replaces Judas.
The Holy Spirit descends on the disciples, and they speak in other tongues. Peter preaches the risen Christ; about three thousand people are baptized.
Stephen, one of the seven, full of grace and power, is stoned while praying for those who kill him. Persecution scatters the believers, who proclaim the Word everywhere.
Philip proclaims Christ in Samaria with miracles. On the road to Gaza, he explains Isaiah 53 to an Ethiopian eunuch and baptizes him.
On the road to Damascus, Saul the persecutor is stopped by the risen Jesus. Ananias lays hands on him; Saul at once proclaims that Jesus is the Son of God.

evenements.titre: Cornelius and the Opening to the Gentiles
evenements.txt: A vision teaches Peter that God shows no partiality. The Holy Spirit falls on Cornelius and his household, Gentiles.
At Antioch, Gentiles are converted; it is there that the disciples are first called Christians. In Jerusalem, Herod has James put to death, but Peter is delivered from prison by an angel.
Sent by the Spirit, Paul and Barnabas evangelize Cyprus and Asia Minor. Churches are born; Paul is stoned at Lystra and survives.
The apostles and elders recognize that Gentiles are saved by grace, without need to be circumcised. A letter is sent to the churches.

evenements.titre: The Second Journey: The Gospel in Europe
evenements.txt: Called by a Macedonian vision, Paul travels into Europe. Lydia believes at Philippi, the jailer is saved; Paul preaches at Athens and stays eighteen months at Corinth.
Paul teaches for two years at Ephesus: all of Asia hears the Word. A riot by the silversmiths breaks out; at Miletus, he bids farewell to the elders of Ephesus.
Accused in the temple, Paul is rescued from the crowd by the commander. The Lord tells him that he will also testify at Rome; he is sent away by night to Caesarea.
Two years in captivity. Paul testifies before Felix, Festus, and King Agrippa, then appeals to Caesar.

evenements.titre: The Journey to Rome and the Shipwreck
evenements.txt: Caught in a storm, the ship is wrecked near Malta; all are saved as God had promised. Paul finally reaches Rome.
A prisoner in a rented house, Paul receives all who come and proclaims the kingdom of God with full boldness. He writes the epistles of the captivity.
In his final letter, Paul declares that he has fought the good fight and kept the faith. According to tradition, Peter and Paul are martyred at Rome under Nero.
As Jesus had foretold, Roman armies destroy Jerusalem and the temple. Not one stone is left upon another.
Exiled on Patmos, John sees the glorified Christ, writes to the seven churches, and beholds the final victory of the Lamb and the new Jerusalem. Come, Lord Jesus!
